therapeutic_hypothesis.intended_biology: restoration of motor function during OFF episodes
therapeutic_hypothesis.target_population: Parkinson's disease patients with motor fluctuations (OFF episodes)
therapeutic_hypothesis.primary_endpoint: Time-matched placebo-adjusted change from baseline in QTcF (ΔΔQTcF) for APL-130277 vs placebo

results.effect_size: Maximum ΔΔQTcF of 6.2 ms (90% CI: 2.7–9.7) at 60 min post-dose; all time points below 10 ms threshold
results.target_engagement_evidence: MDS-UPDRS Part III score improved by up to -31.3 units at 60 min post-dose; median time to ON was 30 minutes
biomarker_changes: Apomorphine Cmax ranged from 4.16 to 9.29 ng/mL across dose levels (10–35 mg)
Apomorphine sulfate Cmax ranged from 220 to 1420 ng/mL across dose levels
Apomorphine Tmax median ranged from 0.75 to 1.50 hours
Apomorphine AUClast ranged from 7.55 to 12.1 h*ng/mL across dose levels
Moxifloxacin positive control showed ΔΔQTcF of 10.0–12.3 ms confirming assay sensitivity
subgroup_findings: Maximum ΔΔQTcF for APL-130277 vs placebo was 6.2 ms (90% CI: 2.7–9.7) at 60 min post-dose, below the 10 ms regulatory threshold
Moxifloxacin assay sensitivity confirmed with ΔΔQTcF of 12.3 ms (90% CI: 7.5–17.1) at 2 hours post-dose
MDS-UPDRS Part III improvement of -26.3 to -31.3 units at 60 min during dose titration phase
Approximately 90% of patients were still ON at 90 minutes (censored) during dose titration
safety_signals: 13/48 patients experienced any TEAE with APL-130277 vs 6 with placebo and 4 with moxifloxacin
12/48 patients had drug-related TEAEs with APL-130277 vs 2 with placebo and 0 with moxifloxacin
1 severe TEAE with APL-130277; none with placebo or moxifloxacin
No serious TEAEs or deaths in any arm

dose_info.dose_modifications: Dose individually determined during titration phase as lowest dose resulting in full ON response or highest tolerated dose

context.indication: Parkinson's disease with motor fluctuations (OFF episodes)
context.comparator: placebo (crossover); moxifloxacin 400 mg as positive control
context.investigator_commentary: This was a thorough QT/QTc (TQT) cardiac safety study. The assay sensitivity was confirmed by moxifloxacin positive control showing ΔΔQTcF >5 ms. APL-130277 did not prolong QTcF beyond the 10 ms regulatory threshold of concern at any time point. Approximately 90% of patients were still ON at 90 minutes during dose titration, indicating durable motor benefit.

results_by_chain.population_description: Parkinson's disease patients with motor fluctuations experiencing OFF episodes
Parkinson's disease patients with motor fluctuations experiencing OFF episodes (positive control arm)
